The exact toy model & what this does not demonstrate

Each ray has pupil coordinate u ∈ {−1, −0.5, 0, 0.5, 1}. Its signed detector error is rᵢ = 0.8 + 1.4uᵢ + 0.22(uᵢ² − 0.5) + A + Buᵢ. Thus ∂rᵢ/∂A = 1 and ∂rᵢ/∂B = uᵢ. A and B illustrate two optical response patterns; they are not calibrated mirror motions.

The LM solve uses residuals r/√5, damping λ = 0.10, and (JᵀJ + λI)Δp = −Jᵀr, with J normalized by √5 too. The aggregate comparison uses the single RMS residual and the same objective and damping. Its Jacobian has only one row. Both formulations have the same objective gradient, but different JᵀJ. A single comparison step is an illustration, not a benchmark of convergence.

This model is linear, so its Jacobian predictions are exact. Real optics require retracing, step acceptance, adaptive damping, and constraint handling. The small curved error pattern cannot be removed by these two controls; the nonzero floor is deliberate. This demo explains conventional ray-residual LM, the foundation of the paper. GTRA additionally creates temporary per-ray targets for a downstream task loss; that extension is not simulated here.

Source: Côté, Tseng & Heide, Generalized Aberrations for Processing-Aware Optical Design, Sections 3.1–3.3, DOI 10.1145/3817055 (the supplied paper).

Built for understanding the off-axis refinement sprint. Synthetic data throughout.
